deep.reconstruction:
Setting. π̂ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}: free profinite on inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_∞, with the single relation l_∞·l_1·l_0 = 1 (the page's ordering convention). Ê^^ = Aut_loc(π̂) is the group of 'local' automorphisms u. Such a u sends each l_i to a conjugate of l_{σ(i)}^p, for some σ ∈ S_3 and some p ∈ Ẑ*. So u respects the set of inertia conjugacy classes up to a permutation and a cyclotomic power.

Purpose. The previous page asked for an explicit extension SΓ_{0,3} of Γ by Ẑ^{{0,1,∞}}, and then SÊ = SΓ ×_Γ Ê by fibre product. This page writes down the profinite group SÊ^^ explicitly.

(1) Elements are tuples ũ = (p, σ, g_0, g_1, g_∞) with p ∈ Ẑ*, σ ∈ S_3 and g_i ∈ π̂.

(2) Two conditions:
- the relation int(g_∞)(l_{σ∞}^p) · int(g_1)(l_{σ1}^p) · int(g_0)(l_{σ0}^p) = 1 holds;
- the three factors generate π̂.
The relation lets the assignment l_i ↦ int(g_i) l_{σ(i)}^p extend to an endomorphism u, as in (3). Generation makes u surjective, hence an automorphism, since finitely generated profinite groups are Hopfian.

(4) Forgetting the g_i but keeping u gives p: SÊ^^ → Aut_loc(π̂).

Geometric meaning. The extra data g_i is a choice of 'path to the cusp i', i.e. a tangential base point at each puncture. It is determined by u only up to the centralizer of l_{σ(i)}, which is the procyclic group generated by it. Hence:
- p is surjective;
- its kernel is {(1,1,l_0^{α_0},l_1^{α_1},l_∞^{α_∞})} ≅ Ẑ^3.
This kernel is the profinite analogue of the three boundary Dehn twists of a pair of pants with boundary. The marginal note 'on retrouve que p est surjectif, de noyau …' records this.

(5)–(6) The canonical map i: π̂ × Ẑ^3 → SÊ^^ is i(g;α) = (1, 1, g l_0^{α_0}, g l_1^{α_1}, g l_∞^{α_∞}).

(7) Hence p∘i(g;α) = int g: inner automorphisms combined with boundary twists.

(8) The group law is ũũ' = (pp', σσ', u(g'_i)·g_{σ'(i)}). It comes from computing u∘u'(l_i) = int(u(g'_i) g_{σ'(i)}) l_{σσ'(i)}^{pp'}.

Next page. Grothendieck remarks that (8) is not fully explicit, because u(g'_i) is only computable when g'_i is given as a word (or limit of words) in the l's. He then derives:
- (9): left multiplication by i(g;α);
- (10): conjugation of i(π̂ × Ẑ^3) by ũ, with exponent ρ (presumably p) and indices permuted by σ.

Overall, this is a 'framed' or 'bordered' version of the automorphism group of the profinite π_1 of the tripod, i.e. the profinite mapping class group of the pair of pants with boundary. It is a building block for his Teichmüller-tower / 'Lego' programme.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. I checked (8) directly: u∘u'(l_i) = int(u(g'_i) g_{σ'(i)}) l_{σσ'(i)}^{pp'}. Formula (9) on the next page is also consistent with (8).
Next page, (9'): the second entry should be 1, not σ. This is a slip.
Next page, (10): ρ should presumably be p.
The page's heading line says multiplication in Ê^^ but means SÊ^^.
Formula (2) depends on the relation convention l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. For odd σ the condition is a genuine constraint, not automatic, which is handled correctly.

ideas.what: Aut_loc(π̂): automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} preserving inertia classes up to permutation in S_3 and a cyclotomic exponent p ∈ Ẑ*
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} preserving inertia (the ambient group of Ihara/Drinfeld's GT̂, extended by S_3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (1979) for the faithful Galois action; Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1991) for GT̂
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981), in spirit; explicit formulas unsure

ideas.what: Extension SÊ of Aut_loc by Ẑ^{0,1,∞}, encoding choices of conjugators g_i (paths to the cusps / tangential base points), with the kernel being boundary twists
ideas.modern_name: Profinite mapping class group of the bordered pair of pants (boundary Dehn twists); automorphisms of the fundamental groupoid with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Drinfeld; Ihara; Nakamura and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for Teichmüller groups with boundary
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions surfaces with boundary and the Lego idea; this explicit group is unsure

ideas.what: Explicit group law (8) and conjugation formula (10) for the framed automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: Standard crossed-homomorphism / semi-direct composition law for automorphisms of the form l_i ↦ g_i l_{σi}^p g_i^{-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; it appears implicitly in GT̂ composition laws (Drinfeld, Ihara)

missed.claim: Already in 1981, Grothendieck explicitly built the profinite 'bordered' mapping class group of the tripod. It is a Ẑ^3-extension of the inertia-preserving automorphism group, including S_3 and the full Ẑ*. He intended to obtain the general SΓ by fibre products. This anticipates the later use of boundary twists and tangential base points in the GT / Teichmüller-tower literature, but is mainly of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: S\hat{\hat{\mathcal E}} \xrightarrow{p} \hat{\hat{\mathcal E}} = \mathrm{Aut}_{loc}(\hat\pi) ... i : \hat\pi \times \hat{\mathbb Z}^{\{0,1,\infty\}} \to S\hat{\hat{\mathcal E}}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the priority and form of Grothendieck's framed-tripod construction, relevant to histories of GT̂ and the Lego-Teichmüller game. Mathematically, it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct but routine. Its content (an automorphism group with conjugator data whose kernel is boundary twists) is well understood in the later GT̂ / tangential base point literature. Interest is mainly historical: an early explicit 1981 form of the bordered-tripod building block.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note: likely reads 'on retrouve que (p) est surjectif, de noyau ... i(...)'. Mathematically the kernel of p is i(1 × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}) ≅ Ẑ^3, not i(π̂). The image of i(π̂ × 1) under p is Inn(π̂).
'La multiplication dans Ê^^' should be 'dans SÊ^^'.
In (2), the first factor is int(g_∞)(l_{σ(∞)}^p); the handwritten 'g_0' was corrected to g_∞.
In (3), the bracketed insertion 'ce qui explicite l'homomorphisme canonique' refers to (4).
